subject: Proposal: High-availability SLA bundles + ramp pricing and surge guardrails
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@acme-systems.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@acme-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: SLA packaging ask + expected ramp / fall-back credits

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We're consolidating the inference stack for a multi-team rollout and need clearer guardrails for high-availability (HA) needs. Two asks from procurement and infra:

1) Can Redwood outline a 3-tier HA bundle (Standard / Elevated / Mission-critical) with explicit response windows, on-call escalation coverage, and per-month uptime targets? We need an example credit table (credits as % of monthly invoice) tied to uptime bands.

2) We expect usage to grow 3–5x over the first 6 months. Procurement wants a ramp discount for committed spend that phases out as usage stabilizes, plus a short-term surge protection policy for accidental bursts during integration.

Attached is a draft operational requirements doc for context. Also open to a quick call next week with your pricing lead and our procurement.

Regards,
Elena
Procurement Manager
Acme Systems

Attachment: Acme-MAP-draft.docx (docx)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@acme-systems.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA packaging ask + expected ramp / fall-back credits

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks and the doc. Happy to map out a compact bundle matrix that shows response windows, escalation tiers (L1, L2, L3 on-call), and the uptime bands with corresponding credit percentages.

High level preview (we'll put this into a single-page table in the formal PDF):
- Standard: 99.5% monthly uptime, 8–24 hour response window, credit up to 5%
- Elevated: 99.9% uptime, 2–8 hour response, on-call L2 escalation, credit up to 10%
- Mission-critical: 99.99% uptime, 30–120 minute response, 24/7 L3 on-call with named escalation, credit up to 25%

For ramping, we can offer a three-month graduated commit discount: 15% off unit price month 1, 10% month 2, 5% month 3 (applies to committed baseline). Surge protection: allow a short burst buffer (20% over commit) billable at a reduced overage rate for first 72 hours during integration windows.

I'll put these into a formal proposal and include the credit math and a sample month-by-month ramp schedule. Can you do 45 minutes on Thu 30 Sep? I'll include our pricing lead (aditya_rao) and solutions (lauren_bennett).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0142

Attachment: HA-SLA-Bundles-v1.pdf (stub)
From: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@acme-systems.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Elena Park <epark@acme-systems.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA packaging ask + expected ramp / fall-back credits

Marcus / Elena —

Thu 30 at 10:00am PT works for me. A couple items to confirm ahead of time so procurement can evaluate:
- Can the uptime bands be evaluated on rolling 30-day windows (not calendar month)?
- For Mission-critical, we require a named escalation contact and an 8-hour runbook handover during SRE on-call swaps.
- For the surge protection, procurement wants a cap on reduced overage pricing (we'd like to see the absolute $/token or $/inference figure, not just %).

If you can include a sample DocuSign-ready SLA appendix, that'll speed legal review.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA packaging ask + expected ramp / fall-back credits

Folks —

Fwd-ing Acme's asks and our quick sketch. They want: rolling 30-day windows, named escalation contact for mission-critical, and explicit $ overage numbers for surge protection.

Proposal I'm leaning toward (please review before the call at 10am PT):
- Uptime measurement: rolling 30-day window (agreeable but increases margin risk; propose tying surge buffer to a 'first-fault' waiver for integration period).
- Credits: revised to a slab table: 99.99–100% = 0% credit; 99.90–99.99% = 10% credit; 99.50–99.90% = 15% credit; <99.50% = 25% credit (mission-critical only triggers up to 25%).
- Ramp discounts: commit baseline defined at contract signature; months 1–3 discount schedule as discussed. Need legal to approve that the discounts are applied to baseline only and not retro to overages.
- Surge cap numbers: propose $0.015 per 1k tokens for reduced overage for first 72 hours, then normal overage rate $0.045 per 1k tokens.

Can you weight in on whether the credit slabs above look too generous? Also attaching a quick pricing workbook that maps these numbers to sample ARR.

Marcus

Attachment: redwood-service-blend-pricing.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@acme-systems.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: HA SLA bundles + ramp pricing (proposal and next steps)

Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the call. Attached is a one-page SLA bundles PDF and a small pricing workbook that ties the ramp schedule and surge cap to example monthly invoices. Highlights and clarifications from today's discussion:

1) Measurement: uptime will be measured on a rolling 30-day window per your request. The SLA appendix includes a short section on clock synchronization and maintenance windows.

2) Escalation & runbook: For Mission-critical, we'll provide a named L3 escalation contact and an 8-hour runbook handover window during on-call swaps. Our on-call roster will be shared with your SRE lead under NDA.

3) Credits: credit slabs (mission-critical example): 99.99–100% = 0%; 99.90–99.99% = 10%; 99.50–99.90% = 15%; <99.50% = 25%. Credits apply as percent of monthly invoice, capped at 25% per calendar month.

4) Ramp discount: commit baseline defined at signature. Month 1 baseline applies 15% discount, month 2 10%, month 3 5% to baseline usage. After month 3, normal pricing applies unless a new commit is negotiated. Discounts do not apply to overage consumption.

5) Surge protection: reduced overage rate of $0.015 per 1k tokens for the first 72 hours of a designated integration burst (max 20% above baseline). After 72 hours or beyond 20% buffer, normal overage $0.045 per 1k tokens applies.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the SLA appendix to the HubSpot deal and share a DocuSign-ready appendix by EOD Monday.
- Please confirm acceptance of the measurement window and surge cap, or list items for legal that need amendment.

If this aligns, I'll convert the attachments into a single DocuSign-ready appendix and route to your procurement.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1-415-555-0142
